rule: Spring tides occur near new moon and full moon
texts: Each Keeper times the salt-bloom harvest to the new-moon spring tide.

fields.sentence: Each Keeper times the salt-bloom harvest to the new-moon spring tide.

q1_issues.issue: "to the new-moon spring tide" is slotted as Goal, but the PP answers none of where/when/how/whence/whither (nothing moves and no destination is stated) — it names what the timing is aligned to, which the instruction set routes to the preposition-named oblique rather than the spatial Goal role.

review.notes: Everything else conforms: "each" rule form with QuantifierPhrase, Patient for the scheduled-occurrence object ("times the harvest" changes when it happens), definite witnesses plus head genus atoms with the noun modifiers left unexposed, and no tense atom on a habitual.

issues.reason: Thematic roles admits the named obliques (Goal included) only when the PP answers where/when/how/whence/whither and orders the parser to "decide by the question the PP answers, never by which listed role is closest" — "to the new-moon spring tide" answers neither whither nor when but names what the scheduling is aligned to, so (Goal (sk_time $x) sk_tide_1) asserts a spatial destination for the timing event that the sentence never states.

new_gaps: a non-purposive entity-argument "to" (align/anchor X to Y) has only one licensed carrier, the preposition-named oblique (To <event> <entity>), and that head is also the purpose connective that seeds (PurposeOf <goal> <event>) — so the compliant form risks deriving a purpose the sentence does not state; the construction needs a carrier the PurposeOf bridge does not fire on
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form is the preposition-named oblique built on the word actually used — (To (sk_time $x) sk_tide_1) — in place of (Goal (sk_time $x) sk_tide_1); no other atom changes.
adjudication.notes: Everything else conforms: the bare-"each" universal as a distributing rule at (STV 1.0 0.9) with its one QuantifierPhrase companion, Patient for the scheduled-occurrence object, both compound kinds carrying head genus only (noun modifiers unexposed), and no tense atom on the habitual.
